# Manual-convention bounty hunt (round: raw GitHub Search, non-platform)

Scope: find MORE projects that manage bounties themselves via a custom
GitHub convention (price in issue title + label), like team113/messenger's
`[$400]` + "help wanted" label — explicitly NOT Algora/Polar/IssueHunt/
Bountysource (other teammates cover those). Search API only, ~14 search
calls + ~15 core calls used, paced within rate limits.

## Method notes (what worked / didn't)

- `label:"help wanted" state:closed` + currency words, and the exact
  team113-style phrases `"looking for freelancer" in:body` /
  `"freelancer to work on" in:body` (re-tried from round 2) — **both are
  dead ends**. 100% noise: Upwork/job-board postings, "hire me" spam,
  generic freelance marketplaces. Zero real project-bounty hits in ~110
  results inspected. Do not re-run these again in future rounds.
- Label sweep `label:paid` / `label:sponsored` / `label:funded` /
  `label:compensation` / `label:freelance` — mostly false positives
  (generic product labels, unrelated "sponsored" tracking labels,
  scientific/software terms). One real hit surfaced: `warpspeedopen-source/
  warpspeed-bounties` (already known/dead from round 1, still just 1
  star, no visible activity — skip again).
- **What actually worked well:** literal `bounty` / `BOUNTY` / `[Bounty:`
  in `in:title`, `is:open`/`is:closed`, sorted by created date descending.
  This surfaces real projects reliably once you filter out the AI-agent
  bounty-farm clusters (very recognizable now: generic titles like "Add
  X guard/helper/utility", `xevrion-v2/agent-playground`, `auscaster/
  frantic-board`, `ritesh-1918/HELPDESK.AI`, `zhangjiayang6835-cyber/
  ai-research`, `dwebagents/AgentPipe`, `9904099`/`123a-bcd` clusters from
  earlier rounds — all still there, all still fake/farm/honeypot).
- New false-positive pattern this round: **"bot-detection honeypot"
  bounties** — trivial tasks explicitly titled to test whether AI agents
  will bite (e.g. "verify bot detection", duplicate near-identical PRs
  from bot-like accounts within minutes). See Riona-AI-Agent below.
- New false-positive pattern: in-game "bounty" systems (SS13-style games
  often have a literal in-game bounty-board mechanic) — `bounty` in an
  issue title can mean "bug in the game's bounty feature," not "we pay
  contributors." See Monkestation/Vanderlin below.

## Genuine candidates found this round

### 1. tenstorrent/tt-metal (+ sibling repo tt-blacksmith) — real, organized, but currently fully claimed

- https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal — 1,559 stars, pushed minutes
  before this check, not archived. Tenstorrent is a real, funded AI chip
  company (Jim Keller); tt-metal is their flagship open-source SDK.
- Convention: `[Bounty $N]` in issue title + `bounty` label, purely
  in-house (own maintainers manually assign), no third-party platform.
  There's even a merged PR "Add bounty program workflows" showing it's
  an intentional internal process.
- Amounts are **real USD**, and substantial: $500–$10,000 per task (ML
  model bring-up, kernel optimization, tooling). Confirmed via 30 title
  hits combining `tt-metal` + `tt-blacksmith`.
- **The catch: every single currently-open priced bounty already has an
  assignee** (checked all 17 open `[Bounty $N]` issues in tt-metal — 17/17
  assigned; tt-blacksmith similarly, plus several CLOSED ones with a named
  assignee, e.g. `[$1000 Bounty] Training workload for GATv2 on PubMed`
  (#453, closed, assignee St1viG) — real proof of payment/completion
  cycle, competition is just already won by the time it's found via search.
- New bounties appear roughly every 1–3 weeks (newest at check-time:
  2026-06-26, $10,000 "Improve tanh accuracy" and $1,500 "SAM2 bring-up,"
  both already assigned within days of posting). **Worth bookmarking and
  checking tt-metal/tt-blacksmith issue lists on a cadence** — the money
  is real and the volume is high, you just need to catch one within hours
  of posting, not days.
- One oddity: `tenstorrent/tt-metal#21636` "tt-metal builds on rocky linux
  9" carries the `bounty` label but **no dollar amount anywhere in the
  issue** — ambiguous/unpriced, don't assume it pays.

### 2. TauCetiStation/TauCetiClassic — new SS13-fork find, small but real and currently open

- https://github.com/TauCetiStation/TauCetiClassic — 158 stars, pushed
  hours before this check (very active), not archived. Russian-language
  SS13 ("Space Station 13") fork community, similar genre to the
  previously-confirmed SPLURT-Station find but a different, unrelated
  project/community.
- Convention: individual community members (not the org itself) post
  `[Bounty]` issues offering to personally pay whoever implements a
  feature — exactly team113-style, fully manual, no platform, payment
  arranged via Discord DM.
- Confirmed real payment history: issue #4959 `[Bounty] 15$ ...` (a
  logging/timezone fix) — dollar amount explicit, closed
  `state_reason: completed` on 2026-06-24 after a contributor
  (Bakomebandias) was given explicit go-ahead by the poster ("Я разрешаю,
  делай" = "I authorize you, do it").
- **Currently open and unassigned:** issue #14916, `[Bounty] Портирование
  ... base_turf для турфов шаттлов` (port a shuttle-floor mechanic),
  posted 2026-06-16, offering **1500 RUB** (~$18-19 at current FX —
  real fiat currency, just a small amount and explicitly self-deprecating
  about the ruble's weak value; not a fake token). 7 comments so far, no
  assignee. Payment explicitly "after successful merge," contact via
  Discord or the issue itself.
- Assessment: legitimate but very low-value (tens of dollars, not
  hundreds), Russian-language project/communication expected, niche
  community. Same caveat profile as SPLURT-Station (niche gaming, small
  $, but real and currently actionable).

### 3. OrcaSlicer (SoftFever/OrcaSlicer, now org OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer) — real multi-year track record, but nothing priced open right now

- https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer — 14,934 stars, pushed at
  check-time (very active), not archived. Extremely popular open-source
  3D-printer slicer (Bambu/Prusa/Voron/etc).
- Convention: `[Bounty: $N]` in issue title, run informally by a
  community member/sponsor (`johnny-bit`, not the lead maintainer
  `SoftFever` personally, though SoftFever is visibly engaged in the
  threads) — a real recurring practice since at least 2023.
- Confirmed real, closed, worked-on bounties with real dollar amounts:
  `[Bounty: $300]` (2023, Overhang Printable Feature), `[Bounty: $250]`
  x2 (2024/2026), `[Bounty: $100]` x2 (Feb 2026, UI improvements) — one
  of these (#12162, "$100 + bonus, make all filament vendors inherit
  from OrcaFilamentLibrary") has an extensive real thread: multiple
  contributors opened real PRs (#12221, #13586, #13589, #13591-13595),
  the bounty poster discussed "payout rails" directly with a contributor,
  and it was eventually **rescinded** by mutual agreement with SoftFever
  — genuine back-and-forth, not a ghost listing.
- **Currently open:** only one `[Bounty]`-titled issue right now (#14503,
  posted same day as this check, 0 comments, unassigned) — but it's a
  **user's feature request that says "I am not entirely sure of the
  standard protocol for incentivizing features here"** — i.e. no
  committed dollar figure yet, purely aspirational. Not yet a real paid
  task; worth watching in case a real number gets attached, but don't
  treat it as live money today.

## Explicitly ruled out this round (new)

- **David-patrick-chuks/Riona-AI-Agent** (4,222 stars, otherwise a real
  active project) — its `[BOUNTY $50]`/`[BOUNTY $100]` issues are
  literally titled "hello-world test endpoint to verify bot detection" /
  "Add /hello health check endpoint," with a cluster of near-duplicate,
  zero-comment PRs from generically-named accounts submitted within
  hours of each other. This reads as the maintainer's own honeypot to
  see if AI agents will autonomously attempt trivial bounties — not a
  genuine paid task. Skip.
- **fluxerapp/fluxer-meta** (parent app `fluxer` is real & popular, 9,478
  stars) — has real $125-$750 "Dev Bounty" issues, but a bot comment
  reveals these actually run through a third-party site called
  **BountyHub** (`bountyhub.dev`), which is out of this round's scope
  (custom-convention only) and also already has multiple competing
  claimants/PRs per issue (e.g. #2 "Polls - $500" has 5+ people
  attempting it). Flagging only for awareness, not recommending.
- **Monkestation/Vanderlin** (SS13-adjacent fantasy fork, 62 stars,
  active) — "Bounties" in issue titles refers to an **in-game bounty
  board game mechanic** (bugs like "Catatoma bounties not giving
  rewards"), not real-money contributor pay. False positive, same trap
  category as district0x from earlier rounds.
- Reconfirmed still-fake/dead from prior rounds when they resurfaced in
  this round's searches: `xevrion-v2/agent-playground`, `auscaster/
  frantic-board`, `ritesh-1918/HELPDESK.AI`, `zhangjiayang6835-cyber/
  ai-research`, `dwebagents/AgentPipe`, `Scottcjn/rustchain-bounties`
  (custom RTC token, presumed worthless per established pattern),
  `openmetaearth/me-hub` (security bug-bounty category, not feature pay).

## Bottom line

Three genuinely real, currently-active, non-platform manual bounty
conventions found this round, none of them previously documented:
**tenstorrent** (tt-metal/tt-blacksmith), **TauCetiStation/TauCetiClassic**,
and **OrcaSlicer**. None has a perfect "free money right now" issue sitting
unassigned:

- tenstorrent has the most money by far ($500–$10,000) and the most solid
  organizational backing, but everything open is already assigned —
  it needs to be watched and jumped on within hours of a new posting.
- TauCetiStation/TauCetiClassic has one small (~$18), unassigned, currently
  open bounty right now — the closest thing to an immediately actionable
  item this round, but the amount is trivial and it's a Russian-language
  niche gaming community.
- OrcaSlicer has the best proven multi-year track record of real $100-$300
  payouts, but nothing priced is open today.

Recommendation: if pursuing further, the highest-leverage next step is
polling tenstorrent's tt-metal/tt-blacksmith issue trackers frequently
(new bounties get assigned within days), rather than continuing broad
GitHub-wide keyword sweeps — the keyword-sweep approach is now heavily
saturated with AI-agent bounty-farm noise and returns diminishing real
hits per search.

## Bottom line up front

**No new candidate that cleanly passes all 4 verification steps was found this round.**
The one borderline item worth logging (lablab-ai/community-content#462) is small
money ($60) and already has an active claimant, so it does not meet the "low
competition" bar cleanly either — logged below for completeness, not as a
strong recommendation.

Archestra-ai (from the previous round) remains the best-documented real,
active bounty source; it just doesn't currently have an open slot either.

## Method this round

1. Pulled `label:"💎 Bounty" state:open` (583 total results) with several
   different sort orders (`created asc`, `created desc`, `comments asc`,
   `updated desc`) and pagination to sample far more of the 583 than the
   ~100 sampled in round 3.
2. Applied GitHub search qualifiers `no:assignee` and `comments:<N` to try to
   automatically surface the least-contested *unassigned* bounties, instead
   of manually guessing org names one at a time.
3. Cross-checked every promising repo's actual open-bounty issues via the
   GitHub REST/Search API (assignee, comments, labels) rather than trusting
   Algora's per-org summary page claim counts.
4. Used WebFetch on algora.io/{org}/bounties for a batch of guessed
   real-company org slugs (dev-tool / YC-ish companies) as a supplementary
   discovery channel. This got 429-rate-limited by algora.io itself partway
   through (see note below) and had to be mostly abandoned in favor of the
   GitHub API approach.

## Full sweep of real (non-farm) repos found with open, unassigned bounties

Every one of these was checked via the GitHub API for assignee status and
comment count. All either have too much existing comment activity/competition,
are stale personal side-projects with negligible payout, or turned out to be
phantom (see next section).

**lablab-ai/community-content#462** — https://github.com/lablab-ai/community-content/issues/462

### 3. New multi-language "AI agent benchmark" farm: UnsafeLabs/Bounty-Hunters

identified in rounds 1-3 (same actor, `UnsafeLabs`, previously seen with

input.content:
# Handover: поиск GitHub-проектов, платящих за закрытие issues

Контекст: искали аналоги team113/messenger (архивирован) — проекты, где
`help wanted` issues реально оплачиваются деньгами. Ниже — что сделано,
что подтвердилось, что не работает, и что осталось незавершённым.

## Хронология и файлы

| Файл | Что внутри |
|---|---|
| `SUMMARY.md` | Первый заход: курируемый список kunovsky, первые находки |
| `REPORT.md`, `results.json` | Сырые данные раунда 1 (298 репо, 111 с issues) |
| `results_round2.json` | Раунд 2: OnlyDust/Bounty0x/Dework, closed-issue поиск |
| `DEEP_REVIEW.md`, `deep_review.json/py` | Скоринг 0-100 по кандидатам — **первая версия была неверной** (см. ниже) |
| `FINAL_VERDICT.md` | Честная ревизия после того, как пользователь поймал ошибку с XTR-токеном |
| `ARCHESTRA_DEEPDIVE.md` | Детальный разбор archestra-ai — лучшая находка, но прямо сейчас пусто |
| `ROUND3_ALGORA_HUNT.md`, `algora_round4_findings.md` | Продолжение охоты по Algora, всё более отрицательный результат |
| `manual_convention_hunt_findings.md` | **Лучший результат за всё время**: tenstorrent, TauCetiStation, OrcaSlicer |
| `polar_hunt_findings.md` | Polar.sh — платформа мертва для этой цели с 2026 года |
| `other_curated_lists_findings.md` | Другие курируемые списки — все нерелевантны/мертвы |

## Что подтвердилось (реальные находки)

1. **tenstorrent/tt-metal + tt-blacksmith** — лучшая находка. Реальная
   AI-чип-компания (Jim Keller), своя ручная конвенция `[Bounty $N]`,
   суммы **$500-$10,000 реальными USD**, подтверждённая история выплат.
   Минус: всё разбирают за 1-3 дня после публикации. Нужно мониторить
   и ловить в первые часы.
2. **TauCetiStation/TauCetiClassic** — SS13-форк, русскоязычное
   сообщество. На момент проверки был один свободный баунти (~$18,
   issue #14916) — маленькая сумма, но реально доступно.
3. **OrcaSlicer** — 14.9k звёзд, многолетняя подтверждённая история
   баунти $100-300. Ничего с ценником не висело на момент проверки, но
   схема рабочая — стоит подписаться и ждать.
4. **archestra-ai** — реальная активная компания на Algora, но все 9
   открытых баунти оказались либо заняты, либо зарезервированы под
   SE-интервью, либо уже имели готовые конкурирующие PR несмотря на
   заниженный счётчик "claims" на сводной странице Algora.
5. **SPLURT-Station SS13**, **Expensify** — подтверждены как реальные
   (настоящие $ суммы), но с оговорками (NSFW-контент / пусто прямо
   сейчас + репутация мгновенного разбора).

## Что НЕ работает (важные негативные инсайты)

1. **Прямой текстовый поиск "$" в GitHub не работает** — токенайзер
   вырезает спецсимволы, запросы вида `"[$" in:title` возвращают 0 или
   мусор.
2. **Слово "bounty" в поиске по GitHub теперь сильно засорено** —
   расплодились кластеры **фейковых баунти-ферм для тестирования
   AI-агентов** (не для людей!). Признаки: репо <50 звёзд с баунти
   >$500, лейбл буквально "Autonomus/Autonomous Agents Only", описание
   репо прямо говорит "sandbox fixture for testing...", репо создано и
   ни разу не пушилось с первого дня, generic auto-generated названия
   issues ("Add X guard/module/assistant" десятками).
3. **"Уже выплаченные, но не закрытые" баунти** — issue помечен как
   открытый баунти, но по факту деньги уже выплачены в 2024-м, просто
   issue не закрыли (bot написал "awarded $X!" в комментах, но лейбл и
   state остались как у открытого). Подтверждено на lablab-ai и
   qdrant/qdrant.
4. **"Баунти-призраки" на удалённые репозитории** — Algora показывает
   открытые баунти на репо, которого уже не существует (404). Всегда
   проверяй репозиторий напрямую через GitHub API, не доверяй сводным
   страницам агрегаторов.
5. **Фейковые репо дословно копируют issue-заголовки настоящих
   компаний** (напр. клон qdrant/qdrant), чтобы выглядеть правдоподобно
   при беглом просмотре.
6. **Algora "claims" counter систематически занижает конкуренцию** —
